entries.measured: read through the port's own note call -charon_noteInterfaceFlags:expensive:constrained:proxy:, which charon_metrics_response makes at NSURLSession.m:676 out of SystemConfiguration, the same question the session already asks before it enqueues. It is the port's own reading of the interface, not a value the release reports about a connection. Not watched on a release either: the only level that could is the 6.1.3 emulator, whose [super resume] is the release's own class, and that probe does not exist.

entries.source: swift-corelibs-foundation's URLSessionTaskMetrics.swift (Apache-2.0) for the shape, and the port's own loader for the values
entries.reason: a literal, by design: the release gives nothing to observe it from. 6.1.3 has no API that reports whether a link is expensive or constrained -- those two arrived with iOS 13 and are the *session configuration's* to say, not the connection's to report -- and whether a connection went through a proxy is the release's own NSURLConnection, which does not say. So the port answers NO, which is the value a release without the signal has, and says so here rather than leaving a reader to believe a measurement was taken

It is the task's own body, which is why a file body answers its size and a stream with no Content-Length answers NSURLSessionTransferSizeUnknown. Not watched on a release either: the only level that could is the 6.1.3 emulator, whose [super resume] is the release's own class, and that probe does not exist.

entries.source: SDK 26.2 headers for what the property is, and the port's own search of its tree for an accessor: NSURLSessionTaskMetrics.m:21 lists it @dynamic and nothing defines it, so there is no code path that could answer it
entries.reason: the data task's transaction is the release's own connection, and its request and response header bytes reach the release's parser and stop there. A stream task cannot stand in for it: it is a raw TCP connection that sends no request and receives no response, so the socket path that closes the other six has no header to count either (facts/Foundation/NSURLSessionStreamTaskSocketMetrics.md, section 4, measures both halves)
entries.effect: the port's class lists the property @dynamic and defines no accessor for it, so respondsToSelector: answers NO for the getter and an unchecked read raises unrecognized selector rather than answering a count

The port records the same number for both on purpose - the release's own connection decodes the body and hands a port nothing it decoded - so this row says that instead of claiming a decoding step that was not measured. entries.source: the port's own stream task over the release's CFStream pair: kCFStreamPropertySocketNativeHandle and getsockname/getpeername for the four names, and kCFStreamPropertySSLContext with SSLGetNegotiatedProtocolVersion and SSLGetNegotiatedCipher for the two values -- all measured in the 6.1.3 armv7 cache with tools/corpus/cache-value.lua, and all reached by name where this library links no CFNetwork and no Security
entries.measured: handed to the transaction by the stream task that owns the socket - NSURLSessionStreamTask9.m:271 calls -charon_noteSocketLocalAddress:port:remoteAddress:remotePort:tlsProtocolVersion:cipherSuite:, and a stream task runs no loader, so the loader is not what makes this one. NOT YET OBSERVED. The only level that could observe these is the 6.1.3 emulator, where [super resume] is the release's own class, and that probe does not exist in this series; the host cannot hold it, because the host's NSURLSessionTask carries -resume mangled to -_onqueue_resume and a stream task cannot be run beside the system's in one process at all (tests/backports/host/streammetrics/ says so in its own header and exits 134 by design). The code is in the library and the 6.1.3 link is green; the measurement is not taken, and this line says so where a porter will read it.
